body: I opened [#120573](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120573) with a likely fix. The crash looks like Vulkan descriptor set/pool churn hitting a driver object limit. The PR adds a small descriptor-set cache and evicts cached sets when their resources/layouts go away. I think I may have fixed it while working on something else in a fork. Can you give it a try?

I don't really know how to compile Godot from source, but if you have a precompiled version with that commit I can give it a try.
Otherwise it might take a while before I have time to learn how to learn how that works, or until it gets added in a dev version.

I force-pushed #120573 to `6893306da0` with a more complete descriptor-set cache key than the first test build (it now keys the actual image views/buffer handles/layouts/sizes/AS handles and evicts on resource/layout free).

The invalid RID / attempted-free lines look like cascade from the failed canvas polygon vertex/index buffers, probably no the main cause.

So I don't want to claim the descriptor-set cache completely fixes this yet. It should reduce one source of Vulkan object churn and may still fix the original descriptor-pool/object-limit path, but if the current PR head still crashes then the next investigation target should be buffer-object/resource churn. The `1920`/`704` byte pair maps well to the Canvas/Polygon2D vertex+index buffer creation path. I thiink this may be the case here too: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118719

Godot v4.7.rc (01db871c5) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21914.8004) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700U with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 15.32 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

Good news: that test confirmed it, and the fix turned out to be tiny.

Plain-English version of what was happening: Godot 4.7 updated the library it uses to hand out video memory, and the new version added a stricter limit check. On AMD integrated graphics that limit is low, so once your project loads enough textures and meshes it trips the check and the engine starts refusing to create anything else; that's the wall of errors and the crash. NVIDIA cards have a vastly higher limit, which is why nobody on those saw it. Switching that one check back off restores the 4.6 behavior.

I've put up a one-line fix, plus a build with just that change so you can confirm it before it goes through review:
https://github.com/vorvek/godot/releases/tag/vma-maxalloc-fix-120534

Open the project the same way; it should just work now.

---

**For the team (technical detail):**

Root cause is the VMA 3.1.0 to 3.3.0 bump (805c9d4b18), which pulled in upstream VMA [`89d3a6a`](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/commit/89d3a6a5ea35d140fe865ed493c89bde777c6a07): it flips `VMA_DEBUG_DONT_EXCEED_MAX_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_COUNT` from `0` to `1`. VMA then returns `VK_ERROR_TOO_MANY_OBJECTS` (the `-10`) once the live `VkDeviceMemory` count hits `maxMemoryAllocationCount` instead of forwarding to the driver. AMD iGPUs report a low count (4096) and this project crosses it on load; NVIDIA's is ~4 billion, hence AMD-only, and D3D12 is unaffected.

It isn't a leak on Godot's side; RD RID counts stay flat/small (confirmed with a probe build). The renderer simply makes >4096 distinct allocations on these GPUs, which 4.6 (VMA 3.1.0, macro `= 0`) tolerated by letting the driver service them. Fix in #120603 defines the macro back to `0`.

I'm also closing my earlier #120573; it cached descriptor sets, but the logs here show every failure is device-memory allocation, not descriptor allocation, so it was aimed at the wrong layer.

Yes, I can confirm that https://github.com/vorvek/godot/releases/tag/vma-maxalloc-fix-120534 works for me.

Thanks for the fix!

FYI, on clayjohn's question in #120603 ("why is Godot causing VMA to exceed the limit"): we measured where the separate `vkAllocateMemory` calls start on a different setup. The trigger looks like VMA's budget fallback.

**Setup:** Godot 4.7.2-stable (official build), Forward+, Linux under WSL2 via Mesa dzn (Vulkan on D3D12), RTX 3070 8 GB. Device-local heap is 7.83 GiB, `maxMemoryAllocationCount` is 65536, so we don't crash, but we see the same allocation explosion. We logged every `vkAllocateMemory`/`vkFreeMemory` through the LunarG `api_dump` layer during a large project's startup. No frames were rendered.

**Measured:**
- Live `VkDeviceMemory` count stays at ~33 (VMA's 256 MiB blocks) until device-local usage reaches ~6.4 GB. Within the next minute it jumps to ~30,000.
- 6.4 GB is 80% of the heap: Godot doesn't set `VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_EXT_MEMORY_BUDGET_BIT`, so VMA uses its 80% heuristic budget (`vk_mem_alloc.h` ~14300).
- At the peak, 23 blocks of 256 MiB plus ~14,400 separate allocations of ≤4 KiB each (128 B to 4 KiB). None are chained with `VkMemoryDedicatedAllocateInfo`, and the driver hinted dedicated for 0 of 179,161 resources.
- `RenderingDevice.get_memory_usage(TOTAL)` reports 3207 MiB. Godot asked the driver for 7346 MiB.

**Why (from the 4.7.2 `vk_mem_alloc.h`):**
- `VmaBlockVector::AllocatePage` only creates a new block if it fits in `budget - usage`, trying 256 MiB down to 32 MiB.
- Once that fails, `AllocateMemoryOfType` falls back to a dedicated allocation. Godot's small-object pools qualify too, since they have `blockSize = 0`, i.e. no explicit block size.
- So past the heuristic budget, every new resource that doesn't fit in an existing block, including each tiny uniform/storage buffer, becomes its own `VkDeviceMemory`.

**Possibly relevant to the AMD iGPU reports (inferred, not tested):** codezero00's report (https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/displayreport.php?id=23906) shows the device-local-only heap 0 is 256 MiB and `maxMemoryAllocationCount` is 4096.
- If Godot's device-local allocations come from that heap, VMA's budget for it is ~205 MiB. Passing that would turn the rest of the load into one allocation per resource and reach 4096 quickly.
- That would also explain why 4.6 survived: before VMA 3.3.0, `VMA_DEBUG_DONT_EXCEED_MAX_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_COUNT` was 0, so the driver accepted counts above the limit.
- `VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_EXT_MEMORY_BUDGET_BIT`, or keeping small-object pools from falling back to dedicated memory (e.g. an explicit pool `blockSize`), may be worth testing there.

**Separately:** on dzn every resource has 64 KiB alignment, and each dedicated allocation is backed by at least 64 KiB. Those ~30k tiny allocations cost ~1.9 GB of real VRAM plus shared memory (Windows per-process GPU counters minus the `vkAllocateMemory` total, which matched live count × 64 KiB at every sample). That part is specific to dzn/D3D12, not Godot.

That solution requires bringing back undefined behavior. I tried implementing a different solution while respecting this "memory allocation limit" but none worked as I wanted. So in the end, we may end up using Vorvek's solution, but we'll need concrete confirmation that the limit is arbitrary and doesn't actually mean anything on AMD drivers.

I think this may be relevant, from upstream VMA: https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/issues/278

For an actual fix, I think we could look into doing the following:
- Enable `VK_EXT_memory_budget` and pass `VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_EXT_MEMORY_BUDGET_BIT`. This replaces the 80% guess with real driver numbers. Also, this may not help on a 256 MiB heap.
- Give the small-allocation pools in `rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp` an explicit blockSize, then those pools never fall back to one dedicated allocation per resource.
- Check which heap Godot’s allocations land on for this iGPU. If most go to the 256 MiB heap 0, steer them to the large host-visible heap 1 instead.
